frontier.hypothesis: The match is one free cse separator away from candidate.c, and the separator does not have to be a store: any construct that makes the +2 read and the p10 read non-equivalent to cse - without adding an instruction or relocating a load - lands the third lw in E2's existing slot-23 nop and byte-matches.
frontier.mechanism: cse merges the two reads because they are structurally identical rtx (mem:SI (plus (reg v1) (const_int 16))). Equivalence, not ordering, is what fails: the load itself is free (the slot is a nop) and every register seat is already target's. Pass attribution should be confirmed against the .cse/.combine dumps before spelling candidates, since the s15 attribution to cse was made on a different spine.
frontier.next_probe: Run pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80060A68 on the E2 body and read tmp/grind/func_80060A68/dumps/*.cse and *.combine to confirm which pass performs the merge and on which rtx. Then sweep ordinary-C spellings that change the rtx of ONE of the two reads without changing the emitted instruction: reading p10 as a different pointer type (u16 * / u8 * / struct *) so its address rtx differs, computing the +2 address as (p-style) base arithmetic that folds to the same lw but a different rtx before cse, and reading through a differently-typed lvalue for outer. Measure build_insns and the three 0x10 load slots/registers for each, and diff any 66-instruction three-load member against target.txt with cmp.sh.

frontier.hypothesis: If R2's window can be satisfied by a donor that is not a gp store, the 0x1A store is freed to act as the second separator and both gaps are covered at zero cost - which is the only other way out of the two-gaps/one-separator bind.
frontier.mechanism: R2 currently requires the D_800A3478 addiu (a span-2 $v0 quantity) inside [+2 read, 0x1A store], which forces the 0x1A store downstream of a gp store while R4 forces every read upstream of it. Any other span-2 quantity that local-alloc allocates before the +2 value and that is live across its two-insn range would push the +2 value to $a0 without a gp store in the window; local-alloc.c:1649-1685 gives a refs-2/span-2 quantity priority 10000, so only a span-2 competitor can win the tie.
frontier.next_probe: Pull tools/ra_solver/local_extract.py text1b --func func_80060A68 (QTYDBG) for E2 and X2, list every quantity with refs, span, priority, allocation order and got, and identify which quantities are span-2 at local-alloc time (post-sched1). Then spell bodies that place a candidate span-2 quantity (the +0 value on the split-0x18 spine, temp0; the idx read; a copy's value) across the +2 value's range without a gp store in the window, and read the +2 value's got field back out of QTYDBG. Bank the dumps under tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s20/.

frontier.hypothesis: The X2 spine (65 instructions, score 4) is a second, cheaper attack surface than E2 for the same defect, because its missing load is the +2 read's rather than the p10 read's and its gap is between two adjacent halfword statements rather than across the p10 read.
frontier.mechanism: X2 spends the free 0x18 separator on the +2-to-p10 gap and leaves the +0/+2 gap open. The two reads there are adjacent statements with no intervening statement at all, so any zero-instruction construct placed between them - including one that is not a store, if the cse-equivalence attack of frontier item 1 works - is enough, and the rest of X2's stream is already target's.
frontier.next_probe: Diff X2 against target.txt with cmp.sh to enumerate its exact residual slots, then sweep the zero-instruction constructs from frontier item 1 into the S1a/S2 gap on the X2 spine (as well as the E2 spine), measuring build_insns and load slots for each. If any member reaches 66 instructions with three loads at 11/19/22, diff it slot-for-slot before scoring conclusions.
